problems.text: match graph: zeros -1; holes -4; asymptotes x = 1 (down, up), y = 1; options a: (x + 4)(x + 1) over (x + 4)(x - 1) | b: -(x + 1)(x - 1) over (x + 4)(x - 1) | c: (x + 1)(x - 1) over (x + 4)(x - 1) | d: -(x + 4)(x + 1) over (x + 4)(x - 1)
problems.explain: It crosses the x-axis at −1, so (x + 1) is on top. It breaks at x = 1, shooting off the grid, so (x − 1) is on the bottom; at x = 1 it goes down on the left and up on the right. The open circle at x = −4 is a hole: (x + 4) is on the top and the bottom, and cancels. Far out it levels off at y = 1, so the top and the bottom have the same degree and the ratio of their leading coefficients is 1. That is (x + 4)(x + 1)/((x + 4)(x − 1)). The others: −(x + 4)(x + 1)/((x + 4)(x − 1)) would level off at y = −1; (x + 1)(x − 1)/((x + 4)(x − 1)) would break at x = −4; −(x + 1)(x − 1)/((x + 4)(x − 1)) would break at x = −4.

problems.text: match graph: zeros -1; holes 4; asymptotes x = -3 (up, down), y = 2; options a: 2(x + 3)(x + 1) over (x + 3)(x - 4) | b: 2(x + 3)(x + 1) over (x + 4)(x + 3) | c: 2(x + 1)(x - 4) over (x - 3)(x - 4) | d: 2(x + 1)(x - 4) over (x + 3)(x - 4)
problems.explain: It crosses the x-axis at −1, so (x + 1) is on top. It breaks at x = −3, shooting off the grid, so (x + 3) is on the bottom; at x = −3 it goes up on the left and down on the right. The open circle at x = 4 is a hole: (x − 4) is on the top and the bottom, and cancels.
